title: A fixed weight closes the one-charge shift exactly when it loses the unbounded charge carrier

weight_dichotomy.definitions: For positive a_n set G_a=sum a_n F_n and S_a=sum a_n sqrt(F_n F_(n+1)) on finitely supported nonnegative sequences
weight_dichotomy.sharp_condition: S_a<=K G_a for some finite K and every F iff M=sup_n a_n/a_(n+1) is finite
weight_dichotomy.necessity: On one adjacent pair the optimal quotient is (1/2)sqrt(a_n/a_(n+1)), so finite K forces the ratios uniformly bounded
weight_dichotomy.spectral_cost: If a_n/a_(n+1)<=M then a_n>=a_0 M^(-n), hence W_a(q)=sum a_n q^(2n) diverges whenever q^2>=M
weight_dichotomy.conclusion: No fixed positive no-loss weight both absorbs the one-step shift and is finite on every charge of an unbounded spectrum
weight_dichotomy.ceiling: Time-dependent weights, cancellations, coupled spacetime norms and non-diagonal energies remain outside the theorem
